lessons.title: Investigating a revenue exception
lessons.html:
A test has produced a hit worth pursuing. What happens next determines whether you end with a finding, a dismissal, or a destroyed case — and most of it is decided in the first hour.

Establish the facts from the data before speaking to anyone. The document and its version history. The surrounding transactions on that till and shift. The stock consequence. The cash consequence. Whether it is isolated or one of a series by the same person. All of this is available without alerting anybody, and going into a conversation already knowing it changes the conversation entirely.

Build the corroboration. A single anomalous transaction is almost always explicable. What makes a finding is the combination: the void, the missing stock at the next count, the cash variance on the same shift, and the pattern repeating across four weeks. Any one of those alone will be explained away, and reasonably so.

Quantify it. "Elevated void rate" is a concern. "₦2.4m of voided transactions in eleven months, of which ₦1.9m had no replacement, at a branch whose shrinkage over the same period was ₦2.1m" is a finding. The number is what moves it from a discussion about behaviour to a decision about action.

Preserve before you disturb. Export and retain the evidence with its definition, as module 2 required. Once anybody knows they are being examined, documents can be amended, explanations constructed, and behaviour changed. The version history will record amendments — but you want the position as it was, held by you, before that happens.

The first hour when the pattern suggests fraud rather than error. Four things, and they are the ones auditors most often get wrong.

Do not tip off. Not a casual question at the branch, not a request for an explanation, not an unusual data request routed through operations.
Do not interview early. An interview conducted before the evidence is complete converts a strong case into a denial and a warning.
Preserve the trail immediately, including anything that could be deleted or amended.
Tell the right person, once. Whoever your charter names — typically the audit committee chair or the chief executive, and specifically not the line manager of the person concerned, who may be involved and will certainly be conflicted.

And know where your role ends. You establish what the data shows. You do not conduct disciplinary proceedings, you do not accuse, and you do not decide consequences. Auditors who step past that line lose the independence that made their work credible, and they usually do it from a sense of responsibility rather than ambition — which makes it harder to resist and no less damaging.

What happens if you are wrong. Sometimes the pattern has an innocent explanation you did not anticipate, and it emerges after you have escalated. Handle it plainly: say so in writing to everyone who received the original concern, and record the explanation so the test can be tuned. An auditor who withdraws a concern cleanly loses very little; one who defends a position after the explanation arrives loses the ability to raise the next one. Being wrong occasionally is the cost of looking at all.

IMPLEMENTATION TIP: Agree the escalation route with your audit committee before you ever need it, and write it down. The worst moment to work out who to tell is the moment you have something to tell, and hesitation at that point is what allows evidence to disappear.

checks.q: You have a strong pattern suggesting till fraud. The first hour should be spent:
opts: Establishing the facts from the data and preserving the evidence
checks.why: An interview before the evidence is complete converts a strong case into a denial and a warning.

checks.q: Who should NOT be told first when fraud is suspected at a branch?
opts: The line manager of the person concerned
checks.why: They may be involved and will certainly be conflicted.

checks.q: 'Elevated void rate at Branch 7' becomes a finding when it is:
opts: Quantified, with the stock and cash consequences attached
checks.why: The number moves it from a discussion about behaviour to a decision about action.

questions.q: A POS transaction in ZhiftERP is recorded as:
opts: A Sales Invoice with is_pos set
questions.why: Carrying pos_profile, owner, posting date and time, with lines in the child table.

questions.q: There is no POS-to-ERP reconciliation to perform because:
opts: The till writes directly into the same backend
It is done by the external auditor
questions.why: An advantage of the architecture, and worth stating in the audit plan.

questions.q: Counting POS revenue without regard to is_consolidated will:
questions.why: Once at transaction level and once consolidated.

questions.q: A cashier's shift is bracketed by:
opts: POS Opening Entry and POS Closing Entry
questions.why: The closing entry carries a payment reconciliation table by mode.

questions.q: A submitted invoice is corrected by:
opts: Cancelling and amending, with amended_from naming the original
questions.why: Which is why a void leaves a full trail rather than a hole.

questions.q: The shape most indicative of till theft is:
opts: A cancellation with no amendment following
An amendment with a lower value
questions.why: A genuine correction produces a replacement; a theft does not.

questions.q: A voided sale where goods physically left creates:
opts: System stock that does not exist, surfacing later as shrinkage
questions.why: Which makes elevated voids plus elevated shrinkage a far stronger finding than either alone.

questions.q: Which is NOT one of the four void signals?
questions.why: Rate, orphans, value and timing — and the combination matters more than any one.

questions.q: A return is identified in the data by:
opts: is_return set, with return_against naming the original
questions.why: Quantities and values are negative; stock returns and cash leaves.

questions.q: Refunds with an empty return_against are:
opts: A nil-expected test where any row needs explanation
questions.why: The population is usually small enough to examine in full.

questions.q: A refund three minutes after the original on the same till suggests:
opts: The sale may never have been real
questions.why: Both very short and very long intervals are testable against the original's timestamp.

questions.q: Trade credit notes deserve equal scrutiny because they are:
opts: Economically identical to a payment out, and usually less supervised
questions.why: The credit-to-revenue ratio varies far more between salespeople than businesses expect.

questions.q: Discount fields sit on:
opts: The Sales Invoice Item child table
questions.why: So discount testing must query the child table; a document view misses it.

questions.q: Which shipped report finds lines where the discount disagrees with the price arithmetic?
questions.why: It costs nothing to run and almost nobody runs it.

questions.q: The unrequested-discount scheme evades detection because:
opts: It produces no cash variance at all
questions.why: Invoice, till and stock movement all agree; only the discount pattern reveals it.

questions.q: Frequent supervisor overrides should be reported as:
opts: A control that has ceased to function
questions.why: It is the normal process with an extra step.

questions.q: Authorisation of an over-limit discount is enforced by Workflow or by:
questions.why: Establish which your business uses; if neither, that is itself the finding.

questions.q: Which measure exposes lapping?
questions.why: Every individual day reconciles under lapping; the delay is the only sign.

questions.q: A persistent small till OVER indicates:
opts: A process that is not working, and possibly a float for a later short
questions.why: Overs matter as much as shorts.

questions.q: A shift closed by somebody other than the cashier who opened it is:
opts: A control breakdown regardless of whether money is missing
questions.why: Along with sessions closed without a reconciliation.

questions.q: Cash variance is best interpreted:
opts: Alongside voids, discounts and banking speed at the same branch and shift
questions.why: Single indicators mislead in cash work more than anywhere else in this track.

questions.q: A branch with no variance at all for six months warrants:
opts: The same curiosity as a persistent difference
questions.why: Independent counting produces small differences.

questions.q: An unnormalised cashier profile identifies as highest risk:
questions.why: Raw counts rank by hours worked and till busyness.

questions.q: A cashier profile should be described to management as:
opts: Where to look, with position implying nothing on its own
questions.why: Somebody is at the top of any list, including a list of honest people.

questions.q: The stronger signal is a cashier who:
opts: Has moved from mid-distribution to the top over four months
questions.why: Change is what you are looking for, and only a retained series shows it.

questions.q: Comparison should proceed:
opts: Within branch, then branch type, then estate
questions.why: A difference surviving all three is worth investigating.

questions.q: A void rate of 3% is interpretable only against:
opts: The estate mean and standard deviation
questions.why: Thresholds are guesses that age badly; distributions adjust themselves.

questions.q: Flagging at two sigma across twenty branches produces:
opts: No flags in a healthy estate
About one false flag per run by chance
questions.why: Three sigma is usually the better working threshold.

questions.q: Different formats showing different void rates should be handled by:
opts: Grouping by format and comparing within the group
questions.why: The outlier that survives grouping is the interesting one.

questions.q: Which is the more useful finding?
opts: A branch at average but deteriorating four months running
questions.why: The first is probably characteristic; the second is a change with a cause.

questions.q: The composite ranking asks which branches appear:
opts: In the worst quartile on three or more measures
questions.why: It answers where to worry without pretending to answer who is stealing.

questions.q: Cancellations with no amendment are a:
questions.why: Expect a modest steady rate and investigate concentration rather than instances.

questions.q: Sales outside trading hours should first be checked against:
questions.why: Configuration explains this more often than behaviour.

questions.q: A test producing forty hits a month produces:
questions.why: Tune until every row is genuinely examined.

questions.q: A new revenue test should be:
opts: Run privately for a month, then tuned and deployed
Deployed to the live programme immediately
questions.why: An untuned release exhausts goodwill and kills the credibility of every test after it.

questions.q: The innocent explanation for a test must be written:
questions.why: If you cannot describe an innocent hit, you cannot interpret a guilty one.

questions.q: On finding a strong fraud pattern, the first hour is spent:
opts: Establishing facts from data and preserving evidence
questions.why: An early interview converts a strong case into a denial and a warning.

questions.q: Evidence should be preserved before disturbing anything because:
opts: Once people know, documents can be amended and explanations constructed
questions.why: You want the position as it was, held by you.

questions.q: Who should not be told first about suspected branch fraud?
opts: The line manager of the person concerned
questions.why: They may be involved and will certainly be conflicted.

questions.q: A concern becomes a finding when it is:
opts: Quantified with stock and cash consequences attached
questions.why: The number moves it from behaviour to action.

questions.q: The auditor's role ends at:
questions.why: Stepping past it loses the independence that made the work credible.

questions.q: The escalation route should be agreed:
opts: Before it is ever needed, in writing
By the executive at the time
questions.why: Hesitation at that moment is what allows evidence to disappear.
